chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, all from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Does either al-Khul' (divorce by compensation) or al-Mubarat (divorce by mutual disavowal) occur except with purity?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It does not occur except with purity.'

key_terms.خُلْعٌ: Khul' (divorce initiated by the wife in exchange for compensation)
key_terms.طُهْرٍ: Purity (ritual cleanliness, specifically from menstruation in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition of ritual purity required for Khul' and Mubarat divorce in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes ritual purity (taharah) as a strict condition for the validity of Khul' and Mubarat divorces, reflecting the Shia juristic preference for avoiding divorce during menstruation to ensure clarity and propriety. The chain of transmission through Safwan and Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj highlights the reliability of this ruling within the Imami tradition, distinguishing it from other schools that may view it as recommended rather than obligatory.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, and abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, altogether from Safwan, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws, ‘Does either Al-Khul’a or Al-Mubaraat happen except by purity?’ So heasws said: ‘It does not happen except by purity (from menstruation)’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al- Jabbar all from Safwan from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajj aj who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if al-Mubarat (disavowing) or al-Khul‘ can take place without Hayd (menses)-free period. He (the Imam) said, ‘It cannot take place without Hayd (menses)- free period.’”
